docs.text: folks isn't it great that climate change has turned the western Great Lakes region into both Florida and Tornado Alley at the same time

So, basically the western 1/3 of the US, the southeastern US....parts of the Great Plains arguably because of Tornado Alley....what's left to insure then? The Great Lakes, the Upper Mississippi, Mid-Atlantic and New England?
I’m heading out to the Great Lakes region in a little over a month and I’m going to need you all to get these nonstop storms and tornadoes out of your system by then, as I don’t like those.
I'be found that in La Niña years, the Great Lakes states tend to see more severe weather/tornadoes 🌪️

I talked with my wife last night, cleared things in the basement incase we need to grab the digs and shelter. Chance of tornados is small this morning, but later it's greater chance. Hopefully the storm will miss us, it seems to be drawn to the great lakes. But it will hit someone.

As in I don't like that hatched risk for damaging winds or tornado threat as it is. The SPC in Norman, OK has a "we probably will have to increase the risk for the Great Lakes" from slight and enhanced risk probably at some point tomorrow.
Lots of “Great lakes is safe” discourse, and I’m like…have y’all looked at the tornadoes in that area lately?
Great Lakes are the safest, but they have had an increase in tornados which is fking amazing in a bad way

The Great Lakes states get horrendous thunderstorms and tornadoes. I once drove from Lansing to Flint in a horrendous thunderstorm. Had to pull off the road because it rained so hard. Got within a mile of destination and the tornado sirens were wailing; one touched down 1/2 mile from house.
Not Tornado Bluesky making me homesick for the Great Lakes
